# Results — Study 911 (REIT Quality Screen)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — **a
"quality REIT" screen (durable-income equity sleeve, low balance-sheet leverage), holding
the residential/broad-property funds and screening *out* the leveraged mortgage-REIT carry,
delivers a better risk-adjusted return than the broad REIT index, net of costs** — run live
on the actual liquid vehicles: **REZ / VNQ / RWR / XLRE** (equity REITs) vs **REM**
(mortgage REITs, the trap), with **SPY** the equity control and **BIL** the tradable
risk-free. Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce
every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete calendar month; the partial current
month is dropped). Fingerprint `b99a4946b405` (daily total-return panel).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily auto-adjusted (**total-return, net-of-fee**) closes — VNQ, REZ, RWR, XLRE, REM, SPY, BIL (public, no key) |
| Window | daily panel 2005-01-03 → 2026-06-30 (5,406 days), as-of 2026-06-30; common monthly sample **2007-06 → 2026-06 (229 months, 19.1 yrs)** |
| Roles | **VNQ** broad REIT index (benchmark) · **REZ** residential/multisector quality sleeve · **RWR** second broad index · **XLRE** S&P real-estate sector (2015-10+, short) · **REM** mortgage REITs (the trap) · **SPY** equity control · **BIL** T-bill |
| Risk-free | **BIL** (1-3m T-bill ETF) — every Sharpe race is **excess-vs-excess** over a tradable rf |
| Execution / costs | one documented lag: the equal-weight quality book sets weights at the prior month-end close and holds the next month; costs are one-way bps × NAV × turnover per monthly rebalance; the broad benchmark is a single buy-and-hold ETF (fees already inside the net-of-fee tape) |
| Statistics | Newey-West (HAC, 6-lag) *t* on monthly spreads; annualised excess Sharpe; a paired circular-block bootstrap Sharpe-advantage CI; a two-era cut (split 2017-01); daily max-drawdowns; a 20-seed synthetic control |

**Short-history / survivorship — named on the Signal axis.** These sector ETFs are young
(XLRE lists only 2015-10; REZ/REM/RWR from 2007), and the sample is one deep cycle plus the
2020 shock — magnitudes are indicative, not a century of evidence.

## The race — excess-vs-excess Sharpe (all minus BIL, 2007-06 → 2026-06)

| sleeve | excess Sharpe | ann. total return | ann. vol |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| **REZ** (residential quality) | **+0.360** | +6.83%/yr | 20.9% |
| **VNQ** (broad index) | +0.290 | +5.40%/yr | 22.3% |
| RWR (broad, 2nd index) | +0.270 | +4.95%/yr | 22.8% |
| **REM** (mortgage-REIT trap) | **+0.039** | **−1.13%/yr** | 24.2% |
| SPY (equity control) | +0.644 | +10.68%/yr | 15.6% |

Two facts jump out: the residential quality sleeve edges the broad index (0.36 vs 0.29), and
the mortgage-REIT sleeve is a **total-return disaster** — a *negative* 19-year total return
(−1.13%/yr) despite its famously fat dividend, at the *highest* vol of the group.

## Leg 1 — the durable-income tilt (quality REZ vs broad VNQ): thin, not certified

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| REZ − VNQ monthly spread | **+8.7 bps/mo** · HAC *t* = **+0.75** (n = 229) |
| equal-weight quality book (VNQ,REZ,RWR) − VNQ | +2.0 bps/mo · HAC *t* = +0.41 |
| Sharpe advantage (REZ over VNQ) | **+0.070**, 95% CI **[−0.070, +0.202]**, frac < 0 = 0.17 |

The tilt points the **right way** but does **not clear the desk bar**: the spread *t* is 0.75,
the equal-weight quality book is thinner still (t = 0.41, because RWR ≈ VNQ dilutes REZ), and
the bootstrap Sharpe-advantage CI **straddles zero**. And it is not era-robust:

| era | REZ − VNQ spread | HAC *t* | n |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 2007-06 → 2016-12 | +1.4 bps/mo | +0.08 | 115 |
| 2017-01 → 2026-06 | +16.2 bps/mo | +1.09 | 114 |

All of the (statistically insignificant) tilt lives in the second half. The durable-income
premium over the *broad equity-REIT index* is **not established** on this tape.

## Leg 2 — the leveraged-carry trap (mortgage REITs) is structurally real

| sleeve | ann. total return | excess Sharpe |
|---|--:|--:|
| REM (mortgage REITs) | **−1.13%/yr** | +0.039 |
| VNQ (broad equity) | +5.40%/yr | +0.290 |
| REZ (quality equity) | +6.83%/yr | +0.360 |

REM's excess Sharpe (0.04) is **an order of magnitude below** the equity-REIT sleeves, and
its total return is *negative* over 19 years — the leveraged carry (borrow short, hold long
mortgage assets, pay out the spread) is a **yield trap** on a total-return basis. The
REZ − REM monthly spread is **+55.0 bps/mo** (HAC *t* = +1.72), and it is **GFC-concentrated**:

| era | REZ − REM spread | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| 2007-06 → 2016-12 | +92.7 bps/mo | +1.83 |
| 2017-01 → 2026-06 | +17.1 bps/mo | +0.47 |

The trap sprang hardest in 2008 (mortgage-REIT leverage detonating), so the *mean-spread t*
alone does not clear 2; but the **structural Sharpe / total-return / drawdown gap is robust
and mechanical.** The crucial caveat for tradability: **the broad index VNQ already holds
essentially no mortgage REITs**, so avoiding the trap is already done, for free, by holding
the standard broad equity-REIT ETF.

## Risk — the whole complex is high-beta, drawdowns are brutal

| sleeve | daily total-return max drawdown |
|---|--:|
| REZ | **−66.9%** (2007-05 → 2009-03) |
| VNQ | **−73.1%** (2007-02 → 2009-03) |
| REM | **−74.7%** (2007-06 → 2008-11) |
| SPY | −55.2% (2007-10 → 2009-03) |

Every REIT sleeve fell 67–75% in the GFC (vs SPY's −55%). The quality sleeve (REZ) drew down
*less* than the broad index — the one place the "quality" story shows up cleanly — but this is
not a low-risk trade in any sleeve.

## Tradability — the quality book, costed vs buy-and-hold VNQ

The equal-weight quality book is rebalanced monthly (one lag); the benchmark is buy-and-hold.

| one-way cost | gross spread | drag | net spread | *t* (net) | ~ ann. |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 2 bps | +2.0 bps/mo | 2.4 bps/yr | **+1.8 bps/mo** | +0.37 | +0.22%/yr |
| 5 bps | +2.0 bps/mo | 6.0 bps/yr | **+1.5 bps/mo** | +0.31 | +0.18%/yr |
| 10 bps | +2.0 bps/mo | 12.0 bps/yr | **+1.0 bps/mo** | +0.21 | +0.12%/yr |

Costs are *not* what kills it — the gross book edge over VNQ is only ~2 bps/mo to begin with,
and nets to a rounding error (~0.1–0.2%/yr, *t* ≈ 0.3). REZ alone is the stronger single
tilt (+8.7 bps/mo gross) but sits inside a smaller, wider-spread fund and its CI runs through
zero. There is **no incremental edge over the broad index worth banking**.

## Synthetic control — the machinery is unbiased (never market evidence)

A deterministic world with a BROAD index, a QUAL leg = `BROAD + planted edge`, and a TRAP leg
(higher-beta, negatively-drifting leveraged carry):

| world | result |
|---|---|
| null (`edge = 0`), 20 seeds | Sharpe advantage mean **−0.019** (sd 0.052); bootstrap CI **straddles zero in 17/20**; trap correctly flagged **20/20** |
| planted (`+3%/yr`, seed 911) | QUAL−BROAD HAC *t* = **+3.17**; Sharpe advantage **+0.109** (CI low +0.040 clear of zero); trap flagged ✓ |

The estimator recovers a planted quality edge, stays centred at zero on the null, and the
trap detector never misses the inferior-Sharpe leg. *(A faithful-engine / power check only —
never cited in support of the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — MIXED.** Two legs, two answers. **(1) The durable-income tilt is not
  certified:** the residential quality sleeve edges the broad index on Sharpe (0.36 vs 0.29)
  but the REZ − VNQ spread is **+8.7 bps/mo at HAC *t* = 0.75**, the equal-weight quality book
  is thinner (t = 0.41), the bootstrap Sharpe-advantage CI **straddles zero** [−0.07, +0.20],
  and it is not era-robust (t = 0.08 then 1.09). **(2) The leveraged-carry *trap* is real and
  structural:** mortgage REITs (REM) earned **−1.13%/yr for 19 years** at excess Sharpe 0.04 —
  an order of magnitude below the equity sleeves — a mechanical yield trap. But the broad
  index already excludes it, so this is a warning about a sleeve, not an incremental edge.
- **Tradability — FRAGILE.** The one robust action — *avoid the mortgage-REIT carry* — is
  already free inside any broad equity-REIT ETF (VNQ holds ≈ no mortgage REITs). The
  incremental quality tilt over the broad index is too thin to bank: the costed quality book
  nets **~+0.1–0.2%/yr at *t* ≈ 0.3** (costs barely matter — the gross edge is only ~2 bps/mo),
  and the stronger single REZ tilt runs its Sharpe-advantage CI through zero. A real
  distinction (equity vs mortgage REITs), but not a bankable premium over the index you'd
  otherwise hold.
